2) Prompt samples: happy to share 4 anonymized prompt-response pairs — I’ll scrub PHI and send by Thu 29 Apr.

Two asks for you: can the token econ sim include a 60 qps scenario and a conservative cache-hit case (10% and 40% prefix caching)? Also, if you can highlight where batching would materially change the per-token cost (and at what latency tradeoff), that’d help us make a go/no-go decision.

Subject: Re: MAP kickoff — unit-econ validation and close timeline

Emily — thanks for the fast follow. I updated the simulation to include a 60 qps column and two cache-hit profiles (10% / 40%). See token_econ_simulation.csv — short notes inline: 

- Batching: we modeled two batching regimes: latency-optimized (max batch size 8, target latency ~120ms) and throughput-optimized (max batch size 64, avg latency ~350–450ms depending on sequence length). Per-token cost drops ~18%–28% moving from latency->throughput for the same model family in our sim.
- Caching: prefix caching primarily reduces compute for multi-turn dialogs; with 40% cache-hit we saw ~22% token-cost reduction in the sim for Novomed prompt shapes.
- Where it matters: if Novomed needs sub-200ms p99, batching is limited and unit costs are closer to the latency-optimized column. If sub-400ms p99 is acceptable, throughput batching plus prefetch reduces unit cost materially.

I can run an extra sim if you attach the 4 prompt samples — I’ll map realistic token distributions and return updated per-token numbers and recommendation for quantization/variant that keeps quality.

Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Principal Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference
